messages.subject: nested or non-nested
parts:
Hi phil

I have a question about comparing one factor model to two factors mirt models, should I consider these models as nested or non-nested? (from the example you gave in your paper mirt: A Multidimensional Item Response Theory Package for the R Environment, I guess that the 2 models can be considered as nested but your comment in another thread makes me doubt)

another question is about the summary function that transforms the discrimination parameters to traditional factor loadings, should I keep the rule of 0.4 to select the items?

Thanks a lot fot your help

Makram.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: nested or non-nested
parts:
Non-nested, so you can only compare with AIC, BIC, etc, and fit model statistics. And no there is no rule of thumb for a factor loading. Even the original cutoffs had no real basis for being set. It's exploratory data analysis, so use your discretion. 

Phil
